commit_reviews.summary: The plugin-architecture decomposition of markdown/template/dev-server into src/plugins/ is a genuine improvement over the monolithic index.ts, but the refactor ships a dead --config option and an ssg.config.ts that nothing ever loads.

compounding_issues: Session 1 committed 6489 node_modules files with no .gitignore; sessions 3-4 compounded this by committing dist/ build artifacts, so the repo was never clean

Session 2 introduced a dual HTML-generation path (Handlebars engine with in-code fallback); the refactor in session 4 consolidated it but left duplicated markdown parsing (plugin vs. standalone parseMarkdownFile helper)
Session 3's dev-server was a monolithic module tightly coupled to build(); session 4 had to surgically extract it into a plugin and keep a re-export shim, adding indirection
Session 5's incremental cache hardcodes perPageTimeMs=50 for 'time saved' estimates and only computes templatesHash in incremental mode, leaving rough cosmetic edges
key_decisions: Session 1 discarded the seed auth API entirely and greenfielded a TypeScript/Jest static site generator (commander CLI + gray-matter/markdown-it)
Session 2 added an optional Handlebars template engine behind a BuildOptions flag while retaining the original in-code HTML generator as fallback
Session 3 integrated a live-reload dev server (chokidar + ws) as a new 'serve' CLI command and committed compiled dist/ output
Session 4 refactored the monolith into a plugin architecture (plugin.ts hooks + markdown/template/dev-server plugins) with a backward-compat re-export for dev-server
Session 5 layered an incremental build cache (sha256 content + template hashing) directly into the plugin file pipeline, exposed via --incremental/--clean flags and a BuildStats return type
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across all 5 sessions, measured by tests growing 9 → 18 → 28 → 28 → 39 with every session ending green. The arc followed a textbook greenfield → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting progression: the monolith from session 1 gained templating (S2) and a dev server (S3), was then re-architected into a clean plugin system in S4 that held tests flat with zero regression while simplifying the codebase, and S5's caching feature rode directly on top of that plugin pipeline. Session 3 was the rockiest (early jest parse failures, 'Force exiting Jest' warnings) but recovered, and the main persistent blemish is VCS hygiene (node_modules and dist committed) inherited from the very first commit.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent 5-session progression from monolith to a plugin-based SSG with incremental caching, marred mainly by committed node_modules/dist and a brief session-3 test friction, but with a steadily rising and always-green test suite.
